briefs.headline: Exxon beats profit expectations as its refineries cash in on a diesel shortage
briefs.summary: On October 30, Exxon reported adjusted profit of $17.5 billion for July to September, or $4.23 per share, beating the $4.08 per share analysts expected. Most of the jump came from refining (turning oil into fuels like diesel), where profit roughly doubled from the quarter before because fighting in the Middle East and attacks on Russian refineries left the world short of diesel. Profit from pumping oil fell about 20% because oil prices were lower than in the spring. Exxon also raised its quarterly dividend to $1.07 per share and plans to buy back $20 billion of its own shares in 2027.
bull: Profit of $4.23 per share beat what analysts expected, and was up from $3.52 the quarter before.
Refining profit was about $9 billion, up roughly 120% from the quarter before, as its Gulf Coast refineries ran at full speed.
Exxon raised its quarterly dividend (cash paid to shareholders) to $1.07 per share and plans $20 billion of share buybacks (the company buying its own shares) in 2027.
bear: Profit from pumping oil and gas fell about 20% because oil prices averaged lower than in the spring.
The refining boom depends on supply problems from war, which could ease and shrink those profits.
Oil and gas output was flat at about 4.5 million barrels a day.

briefs.headline: Disney stock inches up as it cuts costs and pays big to hire AI workers
briefs.summary: Disney shares were trading near $113 on October 22, up a bit more than 2% from the week before. New CEO Josh D'Amaro is reshaping the company. Disney is merging its TV and streaming teams, raising prices for Disney+ and Hulu without ads, and cutting more jobs to make more money. Disney also agreed to pay $60 million a year to hire 66 workers from Character.AI, an AI chatbot company that has gone bankrupt (meaning it can't pay its debts), while one research firm lowered its guess for where Disney's stock is headed.
bull: In its last quarterly report, Disney brought in $25.25 billion in sales, up 6.8% from a year earlier, and its profit per share beat what experts expected.
Disney's cost cutting and price increases are meant to help it keep more of the money it makes.
Hiring Character.AI's workers and getting rights to its technology gives Disney more AI know-how under its new CEO's plan.
bear: Research firm Arete lowered its price target (its guess of what the stock should be worth) from $88 to $86, about 24% below where the stock was trading.
Disney will spend about $180 million over three years on the AI workers' pay and bonuses to keep them, right after laying off several hundred of its own staff.
Character.AI has faced lawsuits from families saying its chatbots hurt their teens, and one market expert said investors now want to see real results.

briefs.headline: Bitcoin dips below $77,000 as customers pull $3.6 billion from Binance
briefs.summary: Bitcoin fell below $77,000 on Monday, November 2, down about 1.4% for the day, after a weekend high near $78,750. Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange (a website where people buy and sell crypto), reopened withdrawals on November 1 after hackers stole about $6.3 billion on October 29, and customers took out a net $3.64 billion. The FBI says North Korea was behind the theft, the largest crypto hack ever. Bitcoin funds that trade like stocks (ETFs) lost $643 million on October 30, their worst day of the month.
bull: Binance says it has covered about 95% of the stolen money with its own funds and promises to cover all losses.
Binance needs to buy about $1.3 billion of Bitcoin and other coins to refill its reserves, which adds buyers.
One expert says big investors are absorbing the shock and Bitcoin could steady between $76,000 and $80,000.
bear: About $3.24 billion of the stolen money is still in the hackers' hands.
Bitcoin ETFs went from gaining money to losing about $516 million in October.
A US regulator said the hack shows the risk of crypto exchanges based outside the US, which could bring new rules.

briefs.summary: Ethereum (ETH) traded around $2,200 to $2,280 on Monday, November 2, close to its two-month low, as the crypto market dealt with the $6.3 billion Binance hack. Ethereum funds that trade like stocks (ETFs) lost about $1.61 billion in October, their worst month since they started. The hacker used Binance's own approval settings, not a flaw in Ethereum itself.
bull: Experts say the hack was caused by Binance's own security steps, not a weakness in Ethereum.
Binance says it has covered about 95% of the stolen money and must buy Ethereum and other coins to refill its reserves.
Ethereum's big yearly conference, Devcon 8, runs November 3 to 6 in Mumbai and could bring good news for the network.
bear: Ethereum ETFs lost money for 11 trading days in a row and had their worst month ever in October.
The whole crypto market lost about $80 billion in value over the past week.
About $3.24 billion of stolen crypto is still with the hackers, who could sell it.
